MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The smart plug feels like a useful next step because it would let my existing Echo devices control a lamp, adding a function I do not already have.",
    "The spare microSD cards fit my history of using removable storage and could work with my existing card reader, provided they are compatible with my devices."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The older Echo Dot, Show 5, and streaming sticks duplicate devices I recently acquired without giving me a clear reason to replace them or add another.",
    "The tablet and Echo Auto introduce uses I have not expressed a need for. Using Alexa at home does not by itself make me want a tablet or Alexa in my car.",
    "The larger Show 8 interests me, but my recent Show 5 purchase and stand make another display less useful right now. The memory card bundle similarly includes a reader whose role my current reader already fills."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My recent Amazon device purchases seem to have been taken as interest in almost any Echo or Fire device, even older devices that repeat what I already own.",
    "My repeated computer and storage purchases seem to have been read as a continuing need for more similar hardware, even when I already have the necessary accessory."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent device purchases matter because they have already met particular needs; the generation and function of what I own affect whether another device would be useful.",
    "My Show 5 stand and Harmony replacement batteries suggest that extending and maintaining equipment I already use can be more appealing than buying another main device.",
    "An accessory is appealing when it adds a needed capability or usable spare capacity. Compatibility and whether I already own an equivalent accessory affect that decision."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognize my interest in electronics and Alexa, but often confuse equipment I already use with equipment I currently need."
}
